answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every identity post a stake before trading and subjecting identities to random audits of signed task histories. When two personas collude to claim the same work, an audit finds conflicting signatures, burns the dishonest stake, and lowers the reputation of linked accounts. The kernel of trust therefore grows from costly participation: a canyon of fake accounts forces the attacker to finance each one and accept repeated loss, while glacier-scale patience cannot erase the bill.
